title: census.py apply takes a group's phase-2 JSON result and does the bookkeeping the orchestrator now does by hand
goal: census.py apply LOG --group G --from RESULTS.json [--dry-run] validates RESULTS.json against a committed JSON Schema of the phase-2 result (outcomes, new_rows, superseded, gaps, conflicts, foreign_edits) and refuses, naming each, an unknown source id, a file outside the group's owned files, an outcome outside the five, or a new row that kbid.py would refuse; then it adds each new row through kbid.py add (never a CSV writer), sets superseded_by on the old rows, writes the gap and conflict bullets under their topic headings in _gaps.md and _conflicts.md, records the outcomes as census.py record does, runs factdiff.py anchor --file on each edited article, build_index.py and doc2query.py stale, and prints the foreign edits for the orchestrator without applying them; --dry-run prints every write and changes nothing. The schema file is the one the phase-2 brief names and that a headless reader can be given with claude -p --json-schema [DOC S1800].
notes: Premise run 2026-10-10: census.py has no apply command (census.py groups, the same parser, exits 2 with invalid choice), and phase 2 step 3 of .claude/skills/kb-census/SKILL.md has the orchestrator run kbid.py add once per new row, set superseded_by, edit _gaps.md and _conflicts.md, run census.py record, factdiff.py anchor, build_index.py and doc2query.py stale by hand; the 2026-09-26 census superseded 144 sources, so 144 kbid.py add calls were model turns. kb/_self/map.csv gains the schema file's row. The work keeps kbid.py the only writer of _sources.csv rows.
